results.diagnosis: Missing or corrupted base image file in nova image cache
supporting_evidence: All error messages reference the same missing file path: /var/lib/nova/instances/_base/a489c868f0c37da93b76227c91bb03908ac0e742
Errors occurred in rapid succession (3 within 50 seconds), suggesting a systemic issue rather than random file access problems
All errors originate from the nova.virt.libvirt.imagecache component which manages base image files

alternative_causes.cause: Filesystem permission issue preventing access to the base file
Race condition during concurrent image operations
Underlying storage system failure

results.diagnosis: Missing or deleted base image file in nova image cache
supporting_evidence: All error messages reference the same missing file path: /var/lib/nova/instances/_base/a489c868f0c37da93b76227c91bb03908ac0e742
Errors originate from nova.virt.libvirt.imagecache component which manages base images
Consistent error pattern suggests a persistent missing file condition rather than transient issue

alternative_causes.cause: Filesystem corruption affecting the base image directory
Race condition during image cleanup operations
Manual deletion of base image by operator

results.diagnosis: Instance base file corruption or deletion leading to synchronization mismatch between database and hypervisor state
supporting_evidence: Repeated warnings about unknown base file in image cache
Instance power state synchronization mismatch (1 in DB vs 0 on hypervisor)
Both errors occurred within same minute suggesting related timing
Both components (imagecache and compute.manager) handle instance disk state

alternative_causes.cause: Filesystem corruption affecting instance storage
Race condition during instance migration
Unauthorized manual deletion of instance files

results.diagnosis: High volume of POST requests to create servers causing API latency spikes
supporting_evidence: 27 slow responses detected with POST /v2/.../servers operations
Multiple POST requests showing high latency (0.668s, 0.544s, 0.516s)
41 HTTP error responses suggest potential overload conditions
All slow responses originate from same endpoint (nova.osapi_compute.wsgi.server)

alternative_causes.cause: Underlying compute resource contention during VM creation
Network latency between API and compute nodes
Database performance issues during server creation transactions

results.diagnosis: Incorrect API version or endpoint configuration in Nova services
supporting_evidence: All errors are HTTP 404 (Not Found) status codes
Errors occur across both nova.osapi_compute.wsgi.server and nova.metadata.wsgi.server components
Pattern includes both GET requests for user_data and POST requests for os-server-external-events
Requests reference API version '2013-10-17' which may be outdated
Project ID 'e9746973ac574c6b8a9e8857f56a7608' appears in failing POST requests

alternative_causes.cause: Misconfigured load balancer routing requests to wrong endpoints
Temporary service degradation during API version upgrade
Incorrect client configuration using deprecated API versions

results.diagnosis: Disk capacity reporting inconsistency - reported disk usage exceeds total capacity
supporting_evidence: Multiple samples show disk usage (20GB) exceeding total capacity (15GB)
Consistent pattern across all 9 high utilization alerts
RAM utilization normal (4%) while disk shows impossible overutilization

alternative_causes.cause: Measurement unit mismatch (GB vs GiB)
Filesystem corruption causing incorrect usage reporting
Hypervisor-level disk accounting error

results.diagnosis: Incorrect disk overcommit ratio configuration in nova-compute

alternative_causes.cause: Physical disk failure causing capacity misreporting
Accounting error in disk usage tracking
Malicious activity artificially inflating disk usage

results.diagnosis: High frequency of GET /v2/<project_id>/servers/detail API requests from a single IP (10.11.10.1) causing disproportionate log volume
supporting_evidence: 47% of all logs are E25 events
Identical endpoint pattern (/v2/<project_id>/servers/detail) across all E25 events
Consistent response length (1893 bytes) suggests identical response payloads
Request timing suggests rapid polling (sub-second intervals)

alternative_causes.cause: Misconfigured client application aggressively polling server details
Legitimate bulk operation requiring frequent server detail checks
Load balancer or proxy misconfiguration duplicating requests

affected_services: Potential impact on Nova API performance under sustained load
